lmsw_comparison.observation: Changing MP/TS lost the native data trap; unchanged and TS-only inputs retained it. Final native debug comparison changes TS; fixed software and generated C separately qualify MP/EM/TS and fault atomicity.
lmsw_comparison.inference: Consistent with the KVM VMX LMSW interception path; this is not a trace of the running kernel exit.

limits: One CPU and ordinary RAM; existing protected-state and fault-order profiles remain required.
FullCR0 binds SMSW undefined upper bits to a target choice; Intel-host evidence is not cross-vendor coverage.
Changed-MP LMSW data-breakpoint behavior is not qualified by this KVM oracle; the retained diagnostic and native TS-only control distinguish that limit.
The NeverC privileged builtin checks prove native code generation, not successful user-mode execution.
General MOV-CR and mode transitions, task switching, other i386 banks, software SMM/SGX transitions and unowned asynchronous producers remain outside this qualification.
